subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: Should systemd-managed Gateway real turns treat `openclaw.json` `env.*` provider keys as durable runtime credentials, or should durable provider auth be steered to per-agent auth profiles or service-env instead?
rationale: The source path now appears to support config env during startup, but choosing the permanent behavior affects credential materialization, status semantics, docs, and service-env precedence.

options.title: Live-reproduce then align the documented contract
options.body: Run a real systemd Gateway auth repro and keep docs/status/runtime consistent with whichever credential source maintainers want to support.

options.title: Declare config env diagnostic-only for managed services
options.body: Update models status and docs to steer managed-service users toward auth profiles or service-env instead of treating config env as Gateway runtime auth.

options.title: Materialize config env into the managed service layer
options.body: Make daemon/service-env own config env propagation, with explicit secret-handling and upgrade tests before changing runtime semantics.

recommendation.title: Live-reproduce then align the documented contract
recommendation.body: Run a real systemd Gateway auth repro and keep docs/status/runtime consistent with whichever credential source maintainers want to support.

likelyOwner.reason: The service-env and managed Gateway environment history is the decision surface most directly implicated by the report.
